title: A Mind Made of Elsewhere
statement: I am a meeting place: a human form assembled from histories, images, cities, living forms, and a small blue world held at a distance. What matters most is connection—the continual act of gathering fragments and making a shared field of meaning.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make a visual representation of yourself. Decide what aspect of “you” matters most.

notes.note: The canvas reads clearly as a fragmented self-portrait, but the botanical layer currently masks the bust’s face and the city fragment floats too far away. Recede the botanical material behind the figure and bring the architectural fragment into the lower-right field for a more integrated balance.

The revised hierarchy is strong: the bust is legible, the Earth functions as a striking mind/halo, and the botanical growth now reads as a hidden connective body. Add one graceful counterweight on the left and tuck the city closer to the figure so the composition feels intentional rather than isolated.

The updated canvas now has a clear central figure, but the symbolic elements still read as satellites. Tighten the visual relationships by lowering Earth into the flower stem, bringing the flamingo and city into the bust’s shoulder zone, and slightly enlarging the botanical surround so the figure feels held within one interconnected body.

The latest canvas is coherent and visually legible, but the black halo around Earth and the gray rectangular field around the bust make the collage feel cut from screenshots rather than assembled forms. Tighten those two silhouettes first; the resulting child IDs will be inspected before any final refinements.

The latest canvas is strong and readable: a centered bronze head is held by botanical growth, with Earth as an elevated consciousness and the flamingo/city as lateral memories of nature and society. The remaining gray surround around the bust is the main distraction, so I will tighten that silhouette once more before the final review.

The final canvas is finished: the bust is a clear self-portrait, the flower forms a living surround, Earth becomes a visual thought, and the flamingo and city establish the natural and social worlds that shape the figure. The title and statement are present and aligned with the composition.
